puzzles.title: Flip the Bit
puzzles.hint: Regular computers have a NOT gate that swaps 0 and 1. Is there a button that does the same job?
puzzles.explanation: X swaps a plain 0 and a plain 1, just like the NOT gate on a regular bit. One gate was all it took.

puzzles.title: Make a Blend
puzzles.hint: The target is an even mix of 0 and 1: the bar splits 50/50. Which gate makes a mix?
puzzles.explanation: H blends a plain 0 into an even mix of 0 and 1. That is why the bar splits 50/50. The mix has a plus sign, which is what |+⟩ means.

puzzles.title: Undo the Blend
puzzles.hint: You want to turn a mix back into a plain state. Quantum gates can be undone. What would undo the blend?
puzzles.explanation: H works both ways. It turns a plain 0 into the plus blend, and it turns the plus blend back into a plain 0. Running the same gate again is how you undo it.

puzzles.title: Back to Zero
puzzles.hint: One of these gates changes nothing you can see on a plain 1. Press them both and watch the bars.
puzzles.explanation: X swapped the 1 for a 0. Z could not help here: a plain 1 has no mix to flip a sign in, so nothing visible changes.

puzzles.title: The Hidden Sign
puzzles.hint: Compare the two bars: they already match! Look at the dial instead. The arrow needs to swing to the other side.
puzzles.explanation: Z flipped the hidden sign, so |+⟩ became |−⟩. The bars never moved, because a measurement cannot see the sign. The dial arrow did move, and the sign changes what later gates do. That hidden sign is a big part of what makes quantum special.

puzzles.title: Minus from Zero
puzzles.hint: Two moves are enough. Think about how to make a mix, and where the minus sign could come from. The order matters, so try more than one.
puzzles.explanation: There are two good ways. Flip to |1⟩ with X, then blend with H, and the blend comes out with a minus sign. Or blend first with H, then flip the hidden sign with Z. Either way you used two gates.

puzzles.title: From One to Plus
puzzles.hint: Two moves. Think about what you can do to a plain 1 to get a plain 0, and what you can do to a plain 0 to get a blend.
puzzles.explanation: X turned the plain 1 into a plain 0, and then H blended it into |+⟩. Another way is H first, which gives |−⟩, and then Z to flip the sign to |+⟩.

puzzles.title: The Invisible Twist
puzzles.hint: Try each gate and watch the dial. If the bars and the dial match the target, you are done, even if the amplitudes look a little different.
puzzles.explanation: Y swaps 0 and 1 like X does, but it also adds a hidden twist, so you got i|1⟩ instead of |1⟩. The i sits in front of the whole state and no measurement can ever see it. It is called global phase, so the game counts i|1⟩ as the same state as |1⟩. The i is a special number that just means a quarter-turn twist; you do not need to calculate with it.

puzzles.title: Y Does It Too
puzzles.hint: Only one of these two gates changes |−⟩ in a way you can see. Press both and watch the dial.
puzzles.explanation: X does nothing visible to |−⟩: it only flips a sign in front of the whole state. Y also swaps the 0 part and the 1 part, but it twists them in opposite directions, and that flips the sign of the blend. You land on |+⟩, with a harmless global twist in front.

puzzles.title: Twist, Then Blend
puzzles.hint: You only have two gates, and both orders work. Try each order and compare the dial to the target.
puzzles.explanation: One way: H blends the 0 into |+⟩, then Y turns it into |−⟩ with a hidden twist in front. The other way: Y swaps the 0 for a 1 (with a twist), then H blends |1⟩ into |−⟩. The twist is global phase, so it does not count.

puzzles.title: Down to Zero
puzzles.hint: Two moves. First turn the mix into a plain state, then fix which plain state it is.
puzzles.explanation: H turned |−⟩ into a plain |1⟩, because it undoes the blend with the minus sign. Then X flipped the 1 into a 0. Two gates, and you were there.

puzzles.title: Blend and Sign
puzzles.hint: Remember the lesson: H turns |+⟩ into a plain 0, but H turns |−⟩ into a plain 1. Work backward from the target.
puzzles.explanation: Z first changed |+⟩ into |−⟩, which only moves the hidden sign. Then H turned |−⟩ into a plain |1⟩. If you had used H first you would have landed on |0⟩.

puzzles.title: The H-Z Sandwich
puzzles.hint: Z does nothing to a plain 0 or 1. So make a mix first, where a sign flip shows up. Then turn the mix back into a plain state.
puzzles.explanation: H blended the 0 into |+⟩. Z flipped the hidden sign to make |−⟩. The second H turned |−⟩ into a plain 1. The sign was invisible until the last H made it show up as a real 0 or 1. Three gates with H on the outside works like a flip.

puzzles.title: Sign Flip, the Hard Way
puzzles.hint: X does nothing visible to |+⟩ or |−⟩. But X does flip plain states. Think of a sandwich with the same gate on the outside.
puzzles.explanation: H turned |+⟩ into a plain 0. X flipped it to a plain 1. The second H turned the 1 into |−⟩. Putting X between two H gates does the same job as a Z gate, using only the gates you have.

puzzles.title: The Sandwich in Reverse
puzzles.hint: It is the same sandwich idea as before, but starting from 1. Mix it, change the hidden sign, then un-mix it.
puzzles.explanation: H turned the 1 into |−⟩. Z flipped its sign to make |+⟩. The second H turned |+⟩ into a plain 0. Three gates, with H on the outside, did the work of an X flip.
